parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Use the correct quotient rule [M1; allow the correct product rule on $x(1+\ln x)^{-1}$]. Obtain the correct derivative in any form [A1]. Equate it to $1/4$ and obtain a quadratic in $\ln x$ or $1+\ln x$ [M1]. Reduce to $(\ln x)^2-2\ln x+1=0$, or a 3-term equivalent [A1; condone $\ln x^2$ if later used correctly]. Solve the 3-term quadratic in $\ln x$ for $x$ [M1; working required if the quadratic is incorrect]. Obtain $x=e$ [A1; accept $e^1$]. Obtain $y=e/2$ [A1; exact only with no preceding decimal; accept $e^1/2$ but not an unevaluated $e/(1+\ln e)$]. Total 7.
